correctness.rationale: The de Bruijn closed-walk criterion is necessary and sufficient even on rings of lengths one and two. The deterministic relation automaton has exactly 735 reachable states and 631 accepting states, both recomputed from the literal local rule. Exact integer calculations compare the proposed logarithmic-derivative coefficients through 39 and confirm 735 recurrence identities on indices 40..774. A 735-dimensional Cayley-Hamilton argument proves the recurrence indefinitely; no finite extrapolation is used. The separate direct brute-force check covers all inputs through ring length 16. Proof and executable certificate are embedded in this item.

value.rationale: Rule 73 is a classically studied complex cellular automaton with distinctive barriers and localized patterns, so its one-step loss of state-space information on finite periodic rings is natural and motivated. The theorem gives a complete all-n enumerator, a compact six-polynomial logarithmic derivative, and proof via a reproducible finite-state certificate. It is not a routine finite-size tabulation or a reexpression of the cited 3x3 pattern diversity.
